speaker: Sheldon
text: Hello, Penny. Leonard just left. What would we talk about? We have no overlapping areas of interest, I'm aware of. As you know, I don't care for chit chat.

speaker: Penny
text: I know. I want to talk to you. Can you just let me in?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, all right, but I don't see this as a promising endeavor.

speaker: Penny
text: Okay, here's the deal. We are going to throw Leonard a kick-ass surprise party for his birthday on Saturday.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I hardly think so. Leonard made it very clear he doesn't want a party. Did someone say party?

speaker: Penny
text: He just doesn't know if he wants one because he's never had one.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I suppose that's possible, but for the record, I've never had a threesome and yet I still know I want one.

speaker: Penny
text: Howard, here's the difference. The possibility exists that Leonard could have a birthday party before hell freezes over.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Fine. If I do have a threesome, you can't be part of it. I'm just kidding. Yes, you can. Can you bring a friend?

speaker: Sheldon
text: I think a birthday party is a terrible idea. I envy Leonard for growing up without that anguish. Year after year, I had to endure wearing conical hats while being forced into the crowded and sweaty hell of bouncy castles, not to mention being blindfolded and spun toward a grotesque tailless donkey as the other children mocked my disorientation.

speaker: Penny
text: Okay, sweetie, I understand you have scars that no non-professional can heal, but nevertheless, we are going to throw Leonard a birthday party.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Have I pointed out that I'm extremely uncomfortable with dancing, loud music, and most other forms of alcohol-induced frivolity?

speaker: Sheldon
text: I really don't think that Leonard wants one.

speaker: Penny
text: Okay, here's the deal. You either help me throw Leonard a birthday party, or so help me God, I will go into your bedroom and unbag all of your most valuable mint-condition comic books, and on one of them, you won't know which, I'll draw a tiny happy face in ink.

speaker: Sheldon
text: You can't do that. If you make a mark in a mint comic book, it's no longer mint.

speaker: Penny
text: Sheldon, do you understand the concept of blackmail?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, of course I do. Oh. Yeah, I have an idea. Let's throw Leonard a kick-ass birthday party.
